$comment: Machine-readable practice index. Each card points at the CLAUDE.md tier that OWNS the rule and never restates it at length — the prose stays the single source of truth. `quote` is the machine anchor: `dev-cli check-practice-index` fails when the cited text no longer appears in `source`, so a rule that is edited or deleted cannot leave a stale card behind. A quote (not a content hash) is the anchor because rule churn here is overwhelmingly ADDITIVE — a section hash would fail on unrelated additions, and a gate that cries wolf is a gate that gets bypassed. The gate covers 'the cited text still exists'; whether a summary is still semantically right stays on review, the same split as check-claude-md and check-doc-links.
$admission: A rule earns a card only when it satisfies at least one of: (i) FOREIGN-SCOPE — written in one tree but governing paths in another, so nested-CLAUDE.md auto-loading never delivers it where it applies; (ii) PATTERN-SCOPED — its real scope is a filename pattern that a directory hierarchy cannot express; (iii) NARROW + SILENT — an invariant whose violation is silent and expensive, scoped tightly enough to fire rarely. A rule that applies to everything adds no routing information and stays out. A rule that is FULLY enforced by a deterministic gate stays out too — `gate` beats a card. Excluded on that ground today: the leaf-independence dependency boundary (`@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`), the committed `.skip`/`.only` ban (`local/no-focused-or-skipped-tests`), and primitive artifact existence (`dev-cli check-primitive-artifacts`).

pathCards.summary: Changing a primitive's props, defaults, or behavior obligates updating its `.mdx` design page in the same pass — docs lead, upstream-first.
pathCards.quote: changing props/defaults/behavior obligates updating this page in the same pass
pathCards.gateNote: `dev-cli check-primitive-artifacts` gates that the page EXISTS; that it was updated to match is not mechanically decidable

pathCards.summary: Introducing or changing SHARED vocabulary (a keyframe, `animate-*` utility, token, reusable overlay/motion pattern) obligates updating the owning `docs/design/*` page and its `_demo` gallery in the same pass — a primitive's own `.mdx` does not discharge the spec tier.
pathCards.quote: obligates updating the owning design page **and its `_demo` gallery** in the same pass
pathCards.gateNote: distinguishing shared vocabulary from primitive-local detail is a judgment call

pathCards.summary: Tailwind v4 landmine: bare arbitrary-property utilities such as `[transition:a,b,c]` do not compile in this repo — use an inline `style` binding instead.
pathCards.quote: bare arbitrary-property utilities like `[transition:a,b,c]` do not compile
pathCards.gateNote: fails silently at build — the class simply never generates, nothing errors

pathCards.summary: The filename picks the tier: `Foo.test.ts` isolates the file under test and mocks every project-internal collaborator; `Foo.integration.test.ts` may use real ones, and only when the interaction itself is what is under test.
pathCards.quote: The three test tiers are the same in every language; only the mechanism differs.
pathCards.gateNote: the mock-isolation half is linted; choosing the right tier for a NEW test is not

pathCards.summary: A test must never spawn `git` without pinning BOTH the repository and the environment — an inherited `GIT_DIR` under a git hook makes an unqualified call write into the developer's real repository. Use `initFixtureRepo`/`fixtureGit`.
pathCards.quote: Never drive git from a test with a bare `execFileSync("git", …)`
pathCards.gateNote: a lint rule is proposed in issue #96; the runtime guard only fires at fixture creation, so a new bare call bypasses it

pathCards.summary: The 3 language variants of a README must not diverge in meaning; wording may differ, facts/instructions/links may not.
pathCards.quote: The 3 language variants of any README must stay in semantic agreement: facts, instructions, and links must not diverge across languages, though wording may.
pathCards.gateNote: the gates hold existence/structure plus technical-token parity (every variant names the same inline code spans as the English canonical); the residue this card covers is whether the prose AROUND those tokens says the same thing — never re-report a differing token, the gate already failed on it

diffCards.summary: a test was changed so it can pass without exercising the behavior its title promises (assertions removed or made trivial)
diffCards.quote: a test is inadequate if the important logic can change without failing it
diffCards.gateNote: requires reading the test against the behavior it claims to pin

diffCards.summary: a stub or placeholder silently returns a fabricated success so a check goes green, instead of failing or TODO-ing loudly
diffCards.quote: a placeholder that returns a fake value to turn a check green
diffCards.gateNote: a fabricated value is indistinguishable from a real one to any checker

diffCards.summary: unrelated refactoring, renaming, or polish mixed into an otherwise focused change
diffCards.quote: Don't refactor or polish stable/unrelated code while making a surgical change
diffCards.gateNote: relatedness is judged against the change's stated goal

diffCards.summary: an added or edited CLAUDE.md/doc is contentless boilerplate restating generic rules instead of file-specific invariants
diffCards.quote: padding to look thorough is itself a violation
diffCards.gateNote: the gate enforces EXISTENCE only; content quality is explicitly left to review

diffCards.summary: the PR description claims something the change as a whole contradicts (e.g. 'tests added' with no test changes)
diffCards.quote: Never mark work complete if anything was silently skipped
diffCards.gateNote: needs the description and the whole change compared against each other, so it is judged once per pull request over the file manifest rather than once per review group — offered against one group's diff it fires on every group, because a description of the whole change always says more than one part of it does

diffCards.summary: an added code comment or durable name (symbol, file, config key, test title) describes the transient process that produced it — 'temporary', 'for now', 'new'/'old'/'previous', 'replaces X', 'phase/step N', 'WIP' — instead of the end-state behavior it should name (Rule 13); the numeric version/ticket subset is already linted, so report only the fuzzy prose a regex cannot safely match
diffCards.quote: Durable names must describe what a thing _is_, never the transient process that produced it
diffCards.gateNote: the regex-safe subset is gated; the fuzzy prose residue is what this card covers

diffCards.summary: a newly added or edited test only asserts that code ran or returned something (truthy, no-throw, a snapshot of trivia) instead of pinning the specific behavior its title promises, so that behavior could break without failing the test (Rule 8) — distinct from weakened-test, which removes teeth an existing test had
diffCards.gateNote: coverage tools count lines executed, not behavior pinned

diffCards.summary: the diff changes real branching or logic in a source file, yet no test anywhere in the same diff exercises that new behavior — it ships unpinned (Rule 8); report only when the source change is present in the diff and no covering test is
diffCards.quote: a test is inadequate if the important logic can change without failing it
diffCards.gateNote: requires matching a source change to whether any test actually covers it

diffCards.summary: the diff hand-rolls bespoke code for something a language built-in or a dependency already imported in the same diff plainly does — added complexity a simpler rung already covered (Rule 2)
diffCards.quote: walk the ladder and stop at the first rung that meets the requirement
diffCards.gateNote: knowing a lower rung existed requires knowing the stdlib and the installed deps

diffCards.summary: the diff hardcodes a literal value that an existing source of truth could derive at read time, or that should live in one shared named config, instead of climbing derive → configure → hardcode (Rule 14) — flag especially when the same value is duplicated across ≥2 files instead of centralized
diffCards.quote: climb the same ladder as Rule 2, applied to _values_ instead of code
diffCards.gateNote: knowing whether a source of truth to derive from already exists requires reading the surrounding code
